Hi Emily — great questions, thanks. I've attached an annotated mapping (redwood-nist-eu-mapping-annotated.pdf) and a proposed regression-sampling-proposal.xlsx that lays out sampling cadence by model risk tier, trigger types, and acceptance thresholds. High level points below; the attachments have the granular references you can paste into the packet.

- NIST AI RMF mapping: we map our controls to the five core functions with explicit owner links. Example: identity & asset inventory -> runtime model registry (Identify); input/output provenance & telemetry -> auditing pipeline (Detect); inference access controls -> tokens/role-based routing (Protect); anomaly-driven automatic throttling and canary rollback (Respond); snapshot-based recovery & model pinning (Recover). See page 2 of the PDF for the full table.

- EU AI Act: Redwood supports the common mitigations that typically appear for high-risk systems: exhaustive audit logs, human oversight affordances in the Console, pre-deployment evaluation sampling (we hold out a representative sample of prompts for regression checks), and operational monitoring with drift detection. For Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments we provide the same behavioral controls and audit hooks; customers manage their own logging retention and KMS integration — Redwood supplies the exportable evidence bundles and a standardized manifest.

- Regression cadence and sampling: our proposal is tiered by risk. Low-risk models: quarterly sampling (random + post-change smoke tests). Mid-risk: monthly sampling + every major model patch triggers a smoke/regression run. High-risk: weekly sampling + mandatory pre-deployment regression on any model or prompt template change, with a minimum sample size defined per acceptance criteria (see attached workbook). We also recommend continuous metric monitoring with automated alerts and mandatory rollback thresholds for safety/accuracy deltas.

I'm copying Ben and Neha to confirm the operational and compliance details. If this meets what your reviewers need, we can convert the mapping into the exhibit format you prefer and sign an NDA addendum if you'd like the example prompt sets included.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Ben — answers inline:

1) Public exhibit: keep sample-size formulas in the workbook but provide an example row for each tier (e.g., High-risk example: n=1,200 prompts stratified by intent buckets). That keeps our posture defensible while giving procurement something concrete.

2) Audit log retention (defaults): Hosted: 180 days by default (exportable sooner); Dedicated: 365 days retention for enterprise reserved deployments (configurable); Private (on-prem/VPC): retention controlled by customer, Redwood provides export manifest and support for KMS/HSM. We'll state defaults and call out export/long-term archive options.

3) Acceptance metrics: top-1 accuracy delta (absolute) remains the primary gate for generative comparator tests for content fidelity. For safety: we use a dual-threshold approach — safety score threshold + human-in-the-loop review rate if safety regressions exceed a soft threshold. Bias checks: we include demographic parity deltas where applicable and FPR/FNR monitoring for classification tasks. Sampling with prefix caching: our sampling harness reconstructs session-level prompts; we include canonicalized prefixes so samples reflect real-world prefixes and KV cache warm states.

I'll add these to the workbook and draft the FAQ snippet.

- Neha

Tom / Emily — appreciate the rapid review. Short answers and attached one-pager in the Drive link below. Key commitments for the exhibit (plain-English bullets you can paste into the board packet):

- Evidence bundles: Hosted customers can create an evidence bundle via the Console API. The one-click bundle includes last-90 days of audit logs (configurable window), the stored pre-deployment regression artifacts for the pinned model version, and the evaluation prompt set used for the regression run. Bundle output is a downloadable manifest + gzipped artifacts.

- Private/VPC: Redwood provides an audited export tool that generates an identical evidence bundle format; export can be initiated via the local control plane or via a support-assist playbook if the customer has air-gapped constraints. We do not remotely access customer VPCs without explicit documented agreement.

- Regression acceptance (one-page summary):
  * For low-risk models: no >5% absolute degradation in primary metric; safety regressions flagged for review if safety score drops by >10% relative to baseline.
  * For mid-risk models: no >2% absolute degradation in primary metric; safety regressions require human review if >5% change in safety score or if triggered by content-safety heuristics.
  * For high-risk models: mandatory pre-deployment regression with stratified sample (example: n>=1,200) and zero tolerance on safety-threshold crossings; any failure requires immediate rollback and formal incident review.

- Sampling & canonicalization: Regression harnesses reconstruct session context to include prefixes and cached KV states where relevant, ensuring sample fidelity to production behavior. Sampling formulas and example rows are in the attached workbook for the board packet.

- Audit logs & retention: defaults: Hosted=180 days, Dedicated=365 days, Private=customer-defined. All logs are exportable in a standard NDJSON manifest.

Links and artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cRedwood-RFPEvidence (contains one-page exhibit + supporting workbook and annotated mapping). We will also produce a DocuSign exhibit attachment if you want the commitments as part of contract annex HL-EXH-C.

Thanks — Vanessa
